about: Records lane SESSIONS writes, made by make_fixtures.py from one scenario; each validates against the schema named (SPINE's, #368).

fixtures.shows: session.start with no prompt: a root session, idle, with no turn and no unit, at revision 1.
session.start with a prompt: the turn is committed queued with its run already bound, and the session is live with a worker the daemon has not yet seen alive. Nothing has been written to an engine.
The engine's typed acceptance of the input arrived: the turn is running and the worker is alive.
session.steer during a running turn: queued, first in the order, with no delivery yet.
The steer's delivery began: delivering, with its delivery id, written into the turn in progress.
The private binding committed with the steer's delivering, before the write: aimed at the turn in progress.
The engine took the steer mid-turn: delivered, carrying the turn it went into.
session.queue, then queue.update while it is still queued: its revision rose to 2.
The engine yielded and waits for the user; the worker that takes another message is still alive.
At the turn's end the message began the next turn: delivering, with the new turn allocated in its binding.
The binding of a message that begins a new turn: the turn id was allocated before the dispatch.
The engine took it as a new turn: delivered, carrying the turn it began.
A Stop of the session's unit was asked and answered pending: stop_pending, the turn still open, the worker kept. No new turn starts while it lasts.
The Stop was confirmed: the turn in progress is stopped and the session is idle with no unit.
queue.cancel while it was still queued: cancelled, never delivered.
The launch definitely did not start: the turn failed with the refusal's code and the session is idle.
The daemon stopped after delivering was committed and before anything was written: at the restart its outcome is unknown, and it is never sent again.
